automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Explicit visible publication or update timestamp inside this 48-hour window required.

searched_topics: agent and tool security including MCP, plugins, browsers, delegated authority, and autonomous action
identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
threat modeling, red teaming, security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates

wiki_and_federation_checked.routing_rule: Retain only security-specific boundaries, impacts, mitigations, and evidence locally; broad product and practice context remains upstream.

source_collection_method.discovery: GitHub Advisory Database REST API publication-window query followed by public advisory and listed project release or commit references.
source_collection_method.duplicate_check: Searched raw, raw/processed, and docs/wiki for retained CVE and GHSA identifiers; no retained identifier was already captured.

qualifying_findings.title: Jan agent-tools workspace guard bypass through dangling symlinks
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database publication; linked upstream project security advisory and fixed-release reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Jan 0.8.5 through before 0.8.8; agent-tools workspace write/edit guard
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: A malicious repository can use dangling symlinks and prompt injection to cause Jan write or edit tools to write outside the workspace, including user-home paths such as SSH authorized_keys. Release v0.8.8 is referenced as the fix.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Repository content is an agent-tool trust boundary: a prompt-influenced write action must not escape its workspace through filesystem indirection.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Jan product background belongs in ai-wiki; general coding-agent trust-prompt and repository-opening practice belongs in ai-dev-wiki. Retain this workspace-escape vulnerability and fixed-version evidence locally.
follow_up_actions: Confirm that the upstream maintainer advisory and v0.8.8 release notes describe the same remediation during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: Mistral Vibe repository-configured gpg.program execution before trust prompt
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database publication; linked project commit and release reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Mistral Vibe before 3.0.3; project context collection invokes git log
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: A crafted repository can configure gpg.program and log.showSignature so Mistral Vibe startup context collection invokes an attacker program through git log before the user receives a trust prompt. Version 3.0.3 is referenced as the fix.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent startup and repository context gathering are executable supply-chain boundaries, not passive metadata inspection.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Mistral Vibe product background belongs in ai-wiki and coding-agent onboarding practice in ai-dev-wiki; retain this pre-trust repository execution boundary locally.
follow_up_actions: Validate release v3.0.3 remediation wording and determine whether a maintainer-authored advisory exists.

qualifying_findings.title: Mistral Vibe Git filter-driver execution during project status collection
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database publication; linked project commit and release reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Mistral Vibe before 2.25.7; ProjectContextProvider git-status collection
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: A crafted repository can configure malicious Git clean or process filters. Startup git-status collection invokes them with user privileges before a trust prompt; v2.25.7 is referenced as the fix.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Repository inspection by an agent can activate Git content filters before consent or tool approval.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Route broad Mistral Vibe and development workflow context upstream; retain the distinct Git-filter execution boundary locally.
follow_up_actions: Keep separate from CVE-2026-122135 at ingest; reconcile maintainer fix details for v2.25.7.

qualifying_findings.title: Mistral Vibe Windows untrusted git.exe search path at agent session start
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database publication; linked project commit and release reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Mistral Vibe before 2.25.5 on Windows; SessionLogger and ProjectContextProvider process launch
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: A malicious git.exe in the repository root can be executed by Mistral Vibe session-start components before a trust prompt. Version 2.25.5 is referenced as the fix.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Repository-local binaries must not be resolved during pre-trust agent startup.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Route broad Mistral Vibe and coding-agent workflow context upstream; retain this Windows-specific pre-trust executable-resolution flaw locally.
follow_up_actions: Keep distinct from the two other Mistral Vibe advisory records and confirm v2.25.5 release remediation during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: DeepSeek Harness unauthenticated local control plane enables agent tool execution
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database publication; linked project commit and fixed-release reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: DeepSeek Harness before 0.1.2-alpha.2, commit 3e24087; local web-profile HTTP/WebSocket RPC control plane
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Missing control-plane authentication permits another local OS user to invoke agent session prompts and Bash/filesystem tools using configured credentials, observe the event stream, and forge approval responses with values broadcast over that stream. Release dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2 is referenced as the fix.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A local agent UI is an authorization boundary: unauthenticated control and telemetry streams can turn delegated authority and stored model credentials into cross-user tool execution.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: DeepSeek product context belongs in ai-wiki and harness workflow practices in ai-dev-wiki; retain the local-control-plane authentication, approval-binding, and credential-use implications locally.
follow_up_actions: Confirm the maintainer release contains the named authentication and approval-binding changes before claiming exact remediation details.

qualifying_findings.title: RAGFlow Seafile connector server-side request forgery
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database publication referencing public disclosure material; no linked maintainer patch or fixed release
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: InfiniFlow RAGFlow through 0.27.3; Seafile Connector seafile_url handling
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The advisory states that manipulation of the Seafile connector seafile_url can produce remote server-side request forgery. It reports public disclosure and says the vendor had not responded at publication.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: RAG data-source connectors are network-capable retrieval boundaries; unvalidated connector endpoints can expose internal services to externally directed requests.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: RAGFlow product background belongs in ai-wiki; retain this connector SSRF boundary locally and route general retrieval practice to ai-dev-wiki.
follow_up_actions: Seek a maintainer advisory, issue, or fixed release during ingest; do not infer a remediation from the database record.
